security_invariant: Internal serialization placeholders must not collide with attacker-controlled string content or escape string-literal boundaries.
attacker_controlled_source: Object values serialized into JavaScript source text.
missing_or_incorrect_control: The replacement expression accepts placeholder-looking text preceded by an escape backslash, while the process-wide UID is generated from a small predictable space.
sensitive_operation: Replacement of internal markers with raw function, regular expression, date, map, set, or special-value source syntax.
vulnerable_behavior: A marker embedded in an escaped string can be mistaken for an internal placeholder and replaced with raw syntax that breaks out of the serialized string.
fixed_behavior: Escaped placeholder text is left untouched and the marker UID is generated from higher-entropy random bytes.
root_cause: A globally replacing placeholder regex does not distinguish internal markers from escaped attacker-controlled string content, enabling generated-code injection when the UID is guessed.
required_evidence: Trace attacker-controlled values into the serialized JSON.
Show an escaped placeholder match crossing a string boundary.
Show raw syntax substituted into the generated source.
refutation_checks: Check whether generated output is treated only as inert text.
Check whether the placeholder UID is unguessable per value.
